newsitem.title: UK: EMU expectations rise in Italy, Denmark - JP Morgan.
newsitem.headline: EMU expectations rise in Italy, Denmark - JP Morgan.

text.p: Markets expectations of Italy and Denmark taking part in European Monetary Union have risen while the probability of most other European countries joining edged slightly lower, JP Morgan's EMU expectations calculator showed.
The U.S. investment house's method of calculating market expectations of EMU occuring monitors bond yield spreads in the swaps market between participating European countries.
The latest calculation shows the probability of Italy joining rose 5.0 percentage points to 51.0 percent in the five days to Friday, while that for Denmark rose 6.0 points to 40.0 percent.
The biggest decline over the five days was in the UK where the probabilty of its memeberhsip of EMU dropped nine percentage points to 41.0 percent.
Elsewhere, Spain dropped four points to 49.0 percent while Sweden dropped three to 62.0 percent and Belgium dropped one percent point to 99.0 percent.
According to these calculations, however, the market still believes there is a 100 percent chance of France participating in EMU.
The calculator works by assigning a market probability level to each country.
This is derived from the actual swap spread, an in-house assumption of what the spread would be if EMU were not a factor and the expected spread after EMU participation, which is zero.
